doc.title: Larry Ridley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 10, 2003

title: Church music as the fabric of life, and segregated schooling
summary: Music in church was natural everyday life, as with Milt Jackson; he describes growing up under segregation and being a token Black student at a white high school.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Wow. Well those are great statements. And I’m curious as to whether music played a big role in your church? LR; Oh yes.
And did you get involved in that music in your church as a young boy?

Couldn’t help it. It was part of the environment and you didn’t even think of it as some sort of separate component. It was just the fabric of life. As I look back over it as we see the way things are being broken down, oh yes, Milt Jackson came up in the church and he did this and that’s the reason why he’s playing the vibes the way he plays the vibes. Well when he was coming up he wasn’t thinking about that as something separate and apart from — it’s just a part of the everyday lifestyle. You know you’re hearing it all the time. I’m hearing this music. So it was just natural. I’m around all this spiritualism, the various preachers and stuff like that, they’re a part of your community, you know them. You are participating in church activities. It’s just a way of life. And my parents, I’m very blessed that I have such great parents who gave me the opportunity and exposed me. We didn’t have a lot of money but we weren’t wanting for anything in terms of the true, spiritual food. And that’s what counts. And my mother and my grandfather always taught me — because I came up under the heavy racism and segregation and went to segregated schools, all that whole thing. And I was a part of a token group that was allowed to integrate the high school that I went to. And it was based upon what kind of I.Q. that I seemed to exhibit to them and they thought well we’ll let the colored kid in.
